overview.intro:
Chapter 60 covers knitted and crocheted fabric sold by the meter or roll: **pile fabrics** such as faux fur, terry and velour (6001), **narrow knits** up to 30 cm wide (6002–6003), **wide stretch fabrics** with 5% or more spandex (6004), **warp knits** such as tricot, raschel and mesh (6005) and **other knits** — the circular-knit jersey, interlock and rib of 6006. Garments and made-up articles cut from these fabrics are in chapters 61 and 63; coated or laminated knits (other than pile) are in chapter 59. Its **106 tariff lines** carry base rates of 4% to 18.5%; most are 10%.

The extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** — 10% or 12.5% in total for Taiwan, the EU, Japan and Korea, where it replaces a lower base rate — and FTA partners such as **Korea and Israel**, duty-free before 2025, now pay 12.5%. **China pays up to 37.5% more** (25% under List 3 plus 12.5%) on 97 lines. USMCA-qualifying fabric from **Mexico** and **Canada** enters free — except Canadian synthetic interlock and double-knit fabric (6006.31–6006.33), which pays **50%** under Section 338. The U.S. imported **$763.3M** of Chapter 60 fabric in 2025; China supplied 21%, then South Korea and Israel.

productGroups.label: Pile fabrics: long pile (faux fur), looped pile (terry), velour and plush
productGroups.blurb: Knitted pile fabric: long pile made by knitting in card sliver (faux fur, sherpa — 6001.10), looped pile and knit terry (6001.21–29) and cut pile such as velour and plush (6001.91–99). The highest-duty heading: 17.2% for man-made fibers, 18.5% for cotton velour. 11% of 2025 imports.

productGroups.label: Narrow knit fabrics (≤ 30 cm) with 5%+ elastomeric yarn or rubber thread
productGroups.blurb: Knit or crochet fabric no wider than 30 cm with 5% or more elastomeric yarn or rubber thread — elastic tapes and trims sold in the piece. 8.8% for cotton, 8% for other fibers.

productGroups.label: Other narrow knit fabrics (≤ 30 cm wide)
productGroups.blurb: Other knit fabric up to 30 cm wide: knitted bindings, rib trims and narrow tubular knits. Warp-knit open-work (14.1%) is split from other narrow fabric (6.6%–8%) for each fiber.

productGroups.label: Wide knit fabrics (> 30 cm) with 5%+ elastomeric yarn or rubber thread
productGroups.blurb: Fabric over 30 cm wide with 5% or more spandex (elastane) and no rubber thread — the stretch jersey, power mesh and swimwear fabric of 6004.10 (12.3%). 12% of 2025 imports. With rubber thread it is 6004.90.20 (12.3%).

productGroups.label: Warp knit fabrics, including galloon (raschel, tricot, mesh)
productGroups.blurb: Warp knits made on tricot, raschel or galloon machines: tricot, mesh, net, stitch-bonded fabric and insecticide-treated mosquito netting (6005.35). All lines are 10%; China List 3 skips some artificial-fiber lines. 40% of 2025 imports, the largest heading.

productGroups.label: Other knitted fabrics: weft/circular knits (jersey, interlock, rib, fleece)
productGroups.blurb: Other knitted fabric — mostly weft or circular knits: single jersey, interlock, double knit, rib and brushed fleece, split by fiber and by finish (bleached, dyed, yarn-dyed, printed). 10% on cotton and man-made fibers. 34% of 2025 imports.

workedExamples.title: Dyed polyester jersey from China
workedExamples.body: Dyed synthetic knit fabric (not double knit or interlock) is 10% at the general rate. China adds 25% under List 3 (9903.88.03) and 12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31): **47.5%** in all, or **$4,750** on a $10,000 shipment.

workedExamples.title: Spandex jersey from Taiwan
workedExamples.body: Weft-knit fabric over 30 cm wide with 5% or more elastomeric yarn is 12.3%. Taiwan's Section 301 rate is 10% in total only where the base rate is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.76), so this line pays its own **12.3%**: **$1,230** on a $10,000 shipment. The same fabric from Vietnam pays 12.3% + 12.5% = **24.8%**.

workedExamples.title: Dyed nylon interlock from Canada, with a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: A USMCA claim removes the 10% base rate and Canada's 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but 6006.32 is on the Section 338 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14), whose 50% applies even to USMCA goods: **$5,000** on a $10,000 shipment entered since August 22, 2026. Without a USMCA claim it is 10% + 10% + 50% = **70%**.

workedExamples.title: Cotton jersey from Mexico, yarn-forward
workedExamples.body: Dyed single-knit cotton fabric is 10% at the general rate. Knit in Mexico from yarn spun in North America from North American cotton, it meets the USMCA rule for Chapter 60 (General Note 11) and enters **free** — no base rate and no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94). Knit from Asian cotton yarn it fails the rule and pays 10% + 10% = **$2,000** on $10,000.

workedExamples.title: Faux fur from China with the product exclusion
workedExamples.body: Long pile knit fabric of man-made fibers is 17.2%. Acrylic pile on a polyester ground valued at no more than $16 per m² is on the China product exclusion list (U.S. note 20(vvv)(iii)(32), 9903.88.69) through November 9, 2026, which removes the 25% List 3 duty but not the 12.5% (9903.05.31): **29.7%** instead of 54.7% — $2,970 rather than $5,470 on $10,000.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Chapter 60 does not cover crochet lace of heading 5804, knitted labels and badges of heading 5807, or knitted fabric impregnated, coated, covered or laminated (chapter 59) — but coated or laminated knitted **pile** fabric stays in heading 6001.

**Note 2.** Fabric of metal thread of a kind used in apparel or furnishings is included.

**Note 3.** "Knitted" goods include stitch-bonded goods whose chain stitches are of textile yarn (statistical lines 6005.36–6005.44, suffix 20).

**Subheading note 1.** 6005.35 is warp-knit mosquito-net fabric of polyethylene monofilament or polyester multifilament, 30–55 g/m², 20–100 holes/cm², impregnated or coated with alpha-cypermethrin, chlorfenapyr, deltamethrin, lambda-cyhalothrin, permethrin or pirimiphos-methyl.

Section XI notes also apply: a blend is classified by the fiber that predominates by weight (note 2), and fabric cut to shape or otherwise made up leaves Chapter 60 for chapters 61–63 (notes 7–8).
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**Additional U.S. note 1.** "Long pile" fabrics (6001.10) are made by inserting fibers from card sliver into the loops of the ground fabric during knitting — the construction of most faux fur and sherpa.

**Additional U.S. note 2.** "Open-work fabrics" have stable open meshes, with or without inwrought designs (the 14.1% lines of 6003 and the suffix-10 lines of 6005).

**Statistical note 1.** "Velour" (6001.92.00.10 and .30) means fabric with 12 or more stitches per centimeter in the vertical direction. The three-digit numbers in brackets (222, 223, 224, 229, 414, 899) are textile category numbers used to monitor shipments.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 60 knit fabric imports since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the end of the IEEPA tariffs and the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs, China List 3 and its faux-fur exclusion, and Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on synthetic interlock.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 106 Chapter 60 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties — up to 50% on Indian and Brazilian fabric — **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on **July 23, 2026**. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**; no Chapter 60 line is on the general exemption list, and only Jordan, and Guatemala and El Salvador for CAFTA-DR goods, have exception lists covering knit fabric. China keeps its 25% List 3 duty, Brazil pays another 25%, and since **August 22, 2026 Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on synthetic double-knit and interlock fabric (6006.31–6006.33).
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 60 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A and the faux-fur exclusion, the Canada Section 338 duty, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. No antidumping or countervailing duty order and no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 60 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03, 25% since May 10, 2019) covers 97 of the 106 lines; 6005.35 (insecticide-treated mosquito-net fabric) is on List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15); and four subheadings — 6001.22, 6005.41, 6006.24.90 and 6006.41 — were only on List 4B, which is suspended (9903.88.16), so they pay the 12.5% alone. The 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) to every line, and China is on no exception list. A product exclusion (U.S. note 20(vvv)(iii)(32), 9903.88.69) removes the 25% from long pile fabric of acrylic pile on a polyester ground valued at no more than $16/m² (6001.10.20) through November 9, 2026. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most Chinese knit fabric pays 37.5% on top of the base rate — 47.5% on the 10% jersey, interlock and warp-knit lines, up to 56% on cotton pile. China shipped $158.7M in 2025.

inEffect.exemption: South Korea's rate is 12.5% in total in place of the base rate when that is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.71). With a KORUS claim (SPI KR) the base rate is Free, so Korean fabric pays 12.5% in total; without one, lines above 12.5% (pile, warp-knit open-work) pay their own base rate. Korea has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Korean knit fabric ($118.3M in 2025) pays 12.5% in total with a KORUS claim — the FTA no longer makes it duty-free.

inEffect.exemption: Israel has no exception list. The U.S.–Israel FTA (SPI IL) makes the base rate Free, but the 12.5% (9903.05.47) applies with or without the claim (U.S. note 52(a)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Israeli knit fabric ($88.2M in 2025, the third-largest supplier) pays 12.5% in total with an FTA claim, where it was duty-free before 2025.

inEffect.exemption: India has no exception list. Chapter 60 lines do not offer GSP. The 2025 IEEPA duties (25% reciprocal plus 25% over Russian oil purchases) ended in February 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian knit fabric pays the base rate plus 10%: 20% on the 10% lines.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(h), 9903.05.94). Under USMCA (General Note 11, Chapter 60 rule) knit fabric qualifies when knit in North America without non-originating materials of headings 5106–5113, chapter 52, 5310–5311 or chapters 54–55 — North American yarn, and for cotton and man-made fibers North American fiber (yarn-forward). Up to 10% by weight of non-originating fiber or yarn is allowed, but non-originating elastomeric yarn only up to 7%. The 2025 IEEPA duty on Mexico (+25%, 9903.01.01) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Mexican knit fabric pays $0 with a valid USMCA claim and the base rate plus 10% without one.

inEffect.exemption: Taiwan's rate is 10% in total in place of the base rate when the base rate is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.76). Every Chapter 60 base rate is at least 4%, and most are 10% or more, so Taiwanese fabric mostly pays only its base rate: 10% on jersey and warp knits, 12.3% on spandex fabric, 17.2% on synthetic pile. Taiwan's exception list (note 52(j), 9903.06.14) names no Chapter 60 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Taiwan ($44.8M in 2025) pays no more than before the 2025 tariffs on its main lines: the base rate, or 10% where the base is lower (some pile lines, the narrow fabrics of 6002–6003, 6004.90.90 and 6006.90).

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(g), 9903.05.93), but the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14) on synthetic knit fabric of 6006.31, 6006.32 and 6006.33 (unbleached, dyed and yarn-dyed, all constructions) applies with or without a USMCA claim; printed 6006.34 is not on the list. No Chapter 60 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian knit fabric pays nothing extra with USMCA, except synthetic 6006.31–6006.33 fabric, which pays 50% (70% without a USMCA claim).

inEffect.exemption: The EU rate is 10% in total in place of the base rate when that is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.39). The EU exception list (note 52(j)(2), 9903.05.97) names no Chapter 60 code. Most Chapter 60 base rates are 10% or more, so EU knit fabric mostly pays its base rate only; lines below 10% — some pile fabrics (6001.10.60, 6001.21, 6001.29, 6001.99), the narrow fabrics of 6002–6003 other than open-work, 6004.90.90 and 6006.90 — rise to 10%. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Italian, German and other EU knit fabric pays its base rate (10%–18.5%), or 10% where the base is lower.

inEffect.exemption: Turkey has no exception list for Chapter 60. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Turkish knit fabric pays the base rate plus 12.5%: 22.5% on the 10% lines.

inEffect.exemption: Vietnam has no exception list for Chapter 60, and Vietnam has no FTA with the United States. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese knit fabric ($19.1M in 2025) pays the base rate plus 12.5%: 22.5% on the 10% lines, 24.8% on spandex fabric (6004.10).

inEffect.exemption: The UK exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(1), 9903.05.96) names no Chapter 60 subheading. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: British knit fabric pays the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Japan's rate is 12.5% in total in place of the base rate when that is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.49); Japan has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Japanese knit fabric pays 12.5% on the 10% and 12.3% lines and its own base rate on pile and open-work lines above 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01, from July 22, 2026) reaches every Chapter 60 line; its exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) names no Chapter 60 subheading. The 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.27). The 2025 IEEPA duties (10% reciprocal and 40%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian knit fabric pays 37.5% on top of the base rate: 47.5% on the 10% lines.

inEffect.exemption: Guatemala's CAFTA-DR list (U.S. note 52(j)(6)(iii), 9903.06.06) covers all 60 Chapter 60 subheadings when CAFTA-DR is claimed (SPI P), and note 52(i) (9903.05.95) exempts CAFTA-DR textile goods entered duty-free. CAFTA-DR's Chapter 60 rule is yarn-forward (General Note 29). 6006.90.90 has no CAFTA-DR rate (its general rate is Free), so it pays the 10%. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Guatemalan knit fabric that qualifies under CAFTA-DR enters free; non-qualifying fabric pays the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (45: Algeria, Angola, Argentina, Australia, Bahamas, Bahrain, Bangladesh, Cambodia, …)
inEffect.exemption: Exception lists in U.S. note 52(j) cover Chapter 60 for Jordan (all 60 subheadings, 9903.06.20) and, for CAFTA-DR claims, Guatemala and El Salvador (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09). Note 52(i) (9903.05.95) exempts CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR. No other country list, and not the general list (note 52(b)), names a Chapter 60 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most other suppliers pay the base rate plus 10% or 12.5%; Jordanian fabric and CAFTA-DR-qualifying Central American fabric enter without the Section 301 duty.

changes.title: No Chapter 60 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 106 Chapter 60 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 60 this keeps +25% (9903.88.03) on 97 lines and +7.5% (9903.88.15) on 6005.35.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 60
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motorcycles from September 29, 2026. No Chapter 60 line is on their annexes.

changes.title: Section 338 list revised; synthetic knit fabric stays on it
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 added and deleted products on the 9903.03.14 list from September 15, 2026, and made the duty apply on top of Section 232 duties. 6006.31, 6006.32 and 6006.33 were not removed; Revision 21 still lists them in U.S. note 51(b)(3).

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on synthetic knit fabric
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods in the provisions of U.S. note 51(b)(3), which include unbleached, dyed and yarn-dyed synthetic knit fabric (6006.31, 6006.32, 6006.33) — 12 Chapter 60 statistical lines. It is charged even when USMCA is claimed and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach every Chapter 60 line
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84); no Chapter 60 subheading is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% and Japanese and Korean goods 12.5% in total, replacing a lower base rate (note 52(k)). Jordan's list covers all of Chapter 60; Guatemala's and El Salvador's cover it for CAFTA-DR claims, and note 52(i) exempts CAFTA-DR textile goods entered duty-free. USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). Other FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 60 subheading is on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) on knit fabric still apply.

changes.title: De minimis suspended indefinitely
changes.detail: CBP's interim final rules suspend the $800 de minimis exemption for every mode (19 CFR 10.151(b), 145.31(b)), so a low-value parcel of fabric needs an entry and pays duty. The suspension has applied to all countries since August 29, 2025 (Executive Order 14324) and was kept after the IEEPA ruling (Executive Order 14388).

changes.title: CBP forced-labor guidance covers cotton knit fabric
changes.detail: CBP's operational guidance for importers lists supply-chain tracing documents for the UFLPA high-priority sectors, including cotton and cotton products and apparel. Cotton knit fabric (6001.21, 6001.91, 6002.40.40, 6003.20, 6005.21–24, 6006.21–24) falls in the cotton sector; the UFLPA presumption applies to any good made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by a listed entity.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 60 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08).

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 60 line; CAFTA-DR-originating fabric is not charged.

changes.title: China faux-fur exclusion extended to November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended 178 China Section 301 product exclusions, including long pile knit fabric of acrylic pile on a polyester ground valued at no more than $16/m² (6001.10.20.00). It removes the 25% List 3 duty (9903.88.69) when the goods match the description.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 60 line on top of the List 3 duty until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: De minimis suspended for all countries
changes.detail: Executive Order 14324 ended duty-free de minimis treatment for shipments of $800 or less from every country, so small fabric orders shipped directly to buyers pay duty.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) over India's purchases of Russian oil, on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all on Indian knit fabric. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 replaced the 10% baseline with country rates, for example India +25%, Vietnam +20%, Thailand +19%, and 15% in total for EU, Japanese and Korean goods. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 (signed July 30, 2025) added 40% on goods of Brazil, on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 60 subheading was on the general exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the List 3 duty on knit fabric.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 60 fabric were **$763.3M in 2025**, -15.7% against $905.6M in 2024 and below the 2022 peak of $1.25B. The top suppliers were **China $158.7M**, **South Korea $118.3M**, **Israel $88.2M**, **India $63.5M**, **Mexico $60.8M**; together they shipped 64%.

By product, warp knits lead: 6005 40%, 6006 34%, 6004 12%, 6001 11%, 6003 4%, 6002 1% of the total (6005 warp knits, 6006 circular knits, 6004 stretch fabric, 6001 pile). The largest six-digit lines were **6005.90** (warp knit fabric of wool or other fibers, $131.7M), **6005.36** (unbleached or bleached synthetic warp knit, $86.2M), **6004.10** (wide knit fabric with 5%+ spandex, $84.6M).

Through 2025 most suppliers paid the IEEPA tariffs on top of the base rate, and China its 25% List 3 duty as well. The IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies instead. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
The total rate on knit fabric depends as much on **where it comes from** as on what it is. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026). **Taiwan and the EU pay 10% in total** and **Japan and Korea 12.5% in total** where that is above the base rate, so their 10% knits pay little or nothing extra; **Israel**, duty-free under its FTA, now pays 12.5%. **Vietnam pays 12.5%** on top of the base rate, **China and Brazil 37.5%**, and USMCA-qualifying fabric from **Mexico and Canada** is free — except Canadian synthetic interlock and double knit (6006.31–6006.33), which pays 50% even with USMCA.

Knit fabric is a textile, so **CBP's textile rules decide where it comes from**: fabric originates where it was **knit** — dyeing, printing and finishing in another country do not change that unless greige fabric is both dyed and printed with two more finishing steps (19 CFR 102.21). Every entry names the knitting mill through a manufacturer identification code. Cotton knits carry UFLPA risk: goods made wholly or in part with Xinjiang cotton are presumed barred.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: knit in **Mexico, Canada or a CAFTA-DR country from regional yarn** (yarn-forward) to remove both the base rate and the Section 301 duty, check whether **spandex content or width** moves the fabric to a lower line, enter **swatches as samples**, and claim **drawback** on fabric that is exported, alone or sewn into garments. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Knit in Mexico or Canada from North American yarn (USMCA yarn-forward)
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 18.5%) and the 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada
levers.appliesTo: All 106 lines, for fabric knit in North America with no non-originating material of headings 5106–5113, chapter 52, 5310–5311 or chapters 54–55 — regional yarn, and regional fiber for cotton and man-made fibers (General Note 11, Chapter 60 rule)
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with SPI "S" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: Up to 10% by weight of non-originating fibers or yarns is allowed (de minimis), but non-originating elastomeric (spandex) yarn only up to 7%. For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 6006.31–6006.33. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS General Note 11 (Chapter 60 rule; textile de minimis)

levers.title: Knit in a CAFTA-DR country from regional yarn
levers.saves: The base rate and the 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: Lines with a CAFTA-DR rate (SPI P — every line except 6006.90.90), for fabric of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras or Nicaragua knit from regional cotton and man-made-fiber yarn (General Note 29: 6001 and 6003–6006 may not use non-originating materials of 5111–5113, chapter 52, 5310–5311 or chapters 54–55; 6002 needs only a change of chapter)
levers.document: A CAFTA-DR claim ("P" before the subheading) based on a certification or the importer's knowledge.
levers.caveat: Note 52(i) lifts the Section 301 duty only for textile goods entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR; Guatemala and El Salvador also have code lists (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09). Elastomeric yarn must be formed in the region. From 2027 Nicaraguan fabric that is not CAFTA-DR-originating also pays 10% (9903.89.01).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)

levers.title: Claim another FTA where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate (4%–18.5%); for Jordan, also the Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: The 105 dutiable lines, for fabric of Korea, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Panama, Israel, Jordan, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman or Singapore meeting that agreement's textile rule; CBERA (E, E*) on some wool, other-fiber and stretch lines
levers.document: Proof of origin under the agreement and the SPI on the entry line (KR, AU, CL, CO, PE, PA, IL, JO, MA, BH, OM, SG, E).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)) — Korea pays 12.5% in total with KORUS — except for Jordan, whose exception list covers all of Chapter 60. No Chapter 60 line offers GSP or AGOA.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a), (j)(13)

levers.title: Check width, spandex content and construction before you buy
levers.saves: Up to 8.5 points of base rate — for example 12.3% (6004.10, 5%+ spandex) vs. 10% (6006) for the same knit with under 5% spandex, or 17.2% (6001.92 pile) vs. 10% (6006.32) for a brushed knit without a pile
levers.appliesTo: Stretch fabrics near the 5% elastomeric threshold, fleece and velour (pile or not), fabric near 30 cm wide, and coated knits (chapter 59 vs. 60)
levers.document: A binding ruling request to CBP with fiber content by weight, construction, width and finish (19 CFR part 177); invoices must show the same fiber content (19 CFR 141.89).
levers.caveat: Change the product only for real commercial reasons — CBP classifies what is imported, and Section 301, 338 and USMCA outcomes also follow the line.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 60 and Section XI notes

levers.title: Claim the China exclusion for acrylic faux fur
levers.saves: The 25% List 3 duty (the 12.5% 2026 duty still applies)
levers.appliesTo: Chinese long pile knit fabric of acrylic pile on a polyester ground, valued at no more than $16/m² (6001.10.20.00), entered by November 9, 2026
levers.document: Heading 9903.88.69 reported with 6001.10.20.00, and records showing fiber content, construction and value per m².
levers.caveat: Only fabric matching the description qualifies; it ends after November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends it again.

levers.title: Enter swatches and headers as samples
levers.saves: All duty — base rate and the Section 301, China and Canada duties
levers.appliesTo: Fabric swatches and sample cards valued at $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, used only to solicit orders
levers.document: Entry under 9811.00.60 with the samples marked or mutilated as the heading requires.
levers.caveat: Usable sample yardage does not qualify. U.S. notes 20, 51 and 52 exempt goods properly entered under Chapter 98 from those extra duties. De minimis is suspended, so even a low-value parcel needs an entry.

provisions.text: Samples valued not over $1 each, or marked, torn, perforated or otherwise treated so they are unsuitable for sale, used only for soliciting orders for products of foreign countries

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20(a), 51, 52(a)

levers.title: Claim drawback when the fabric, or garments made from it, are exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on fabric re-exported or cut and sewn into exported goods
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported fabric or substitutes are exported or used in manufacturing exported goods
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a specific or general manufacturing ruling.

rules.title: Textile country of origin: knit fabric originates where it was knit (fabric-making process); dyeing, printing or finishing elsewhere changes origin only when greige fabric is both dyed and printed plus two finishing operations, and never for wool fabric
Manufacturer identification code (MID) of the knitting mill that performed the origin-conferring operation, on every entry — this replaced the textile declaration, eliminated in 2011
Entry is denied for textiles from a company named by CITA in the Federal Register for illegal transshipment or for being unable to verify production
Invoice details for textile fiber products: each fiber by generic name and percentage by weight (5% or more), the manufacturer and the country where processed or made
Textile Fiber Products Identification Act: fabric sold onward must disclose fiber content (e.g. "95% cotton, 5% spandex") and country of origin

Flammable Fabrics Act: fabric used or intended for apparel must meet the clothing-textile flammability standard (plain-surface fabric of 2.6 oz/yd² or more and all-acrylic, modacrylic, nylon, olefin, polyester or wool fabric are exempt from testing); raised-surface fabric such as fleece and velour is the main risk

UFLPA and the Xinjiang cotton withhold release order: goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are presumed made with forced labor and denied entry unless the importer rebuts it; cotton knits need supply-chain tracing back to the cotton

Insecticide-treated mosquito-net fabric (6005.35) is a pesticide product: an EPA Notice of Arrival before the shipment arrives, and registration unless exempt (the treated-article exemption covers only a pesticide that protects the fabric itself)
Country-of-origin marking on the article or, for piece goods on rolls or bolts, on its container
No de minimis: a low-value parcel of fabric needs a formal or informal entry and pays duty

groups.label: Pile fabrics: long pile (faux fur), looped pile (terry), velour and plush
groups.note: Pile fabric originates where it was knit. Faux fur, velour and plush are raised-surface fabrics for CPSC flammability if used in apparel. China's exclusion covers only acrylic-on-polyester long pile at ≤ $16/m².

groups.label: Narrow knit fabrics (≤ 30 cm) with 5%+ elastomeric yarn or rubber thread
groups.note: Narrow (≤ 30 cm) elastic knits. Elastomeric yarn must be formed in North America or the CAFTA-DR region for USMCA or CAFTA-DR, beyond the 7% (USMCA) allowance.

groups.label: Other narrow knit fabrics (≤ 30 cm wide)
groups.note: Narrow knits other than elastic. Open-work warp knits (14.1%) are split from other fabric (6.6%–8%) — the construction decides the rate.

groups.label: Wide knit fabrics (> 30 cm) with 5%+ elastomeric yarn or rubber thread
groups.note: Wide fabric with 5% or more spandex (12.3%). Under 5% elastomeric yarn the same knit is 6005 or 6006 at 10%. Non-originating spandex limits USMCA qualification.

groups.label: Warp knit fabrics, including galloon (raschel, tricot, mesh)
groups.note: Warp knits, all 10%. Insecticide-treated mosquito-net fabric (6005.35) needs an EPA Notice of Arrival; made-up bed nets are 6304.20, not this chapter.

groups.label: Other knitted fabrics: weft/circular knits (jersey, interlock, rib, fleece)
groups.note: Circular knits, mostly 10%. Cotton jersey and rib carry UFLPA tracing; synthetic 6006.31–6006.33 from Canada pays 50% under Section 338 even with USMCA.

seo.title: Knitted Fabric HS Code & Tariff FAQ 2026: Jersey, Spandex, Fleece, Mesh, Faux Fur (HTS Chapter 60) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about importing knit fabric: the HS / tariff code for knitted, jersey, spandex, fleece, velour, mesh and faux-fur fabric, the yarn-forward rule, and the 2026 tariffs on fabric from China, Vietnam and Mexico.
keywords: china tariffs on knitted or crocheted fabrics

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing knitted and crocheted fabric into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and origin rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 60 base rates run from 4% to 18.5% — 10% on most jersey, interlock and warp-knit lines, 12.3% on spandex fabric, 17.2%–18.5% on pile — and are unchanged since January 2025. The extra duty by country decides the cost.

Since July 24, 2026 most suppliers pay a 10% or 12.5% Section 301 tariff; Taiwan and the EU pay 10% and Japan and Korea 12.5% in total, so their 10% knits pay little or nothing extra. No Chapter 60 line is on the general exemption list.

China pays 37.5% extra on 97 of 106 lines (47.5% on 10% fabrics); Vietnam 12.5%; Brazil 37.5%. Canada pays 50% under Section 338 on synthetic interlock and double knit (6006.31–6006.33), even with USMCA.
Fabric knit in Mexico, Canada or a CAFTA-DR country from regional yarn (yarn-forward) enters free of both the base rate and the Section 301 duty.

The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. Knit fabric originates where it was knit (19 CFR 102.21); cotton knits must be traceable away from Xinjiang under the UFLPA.

faqs.question: What is the HS code (tariff code) for knitted fabric?
searchedAs: knitted or crocheted fabrics hs code
faqs.answer: Knitted and crocheted fabric is HTS Chapter 60, headings 6001–6006: 6001 pile fabrics, 6002 and 6003 fabric no wider than 30 cm, 6004 fabric over 30 cm with 5% or more elastomeric yarn, 6005 warp knits and 6006 other knits. The first six digits are the same in every country's HS schedule; the U.S. adds four more. Base rates run from 4% to 18.5%, mostly 10%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for polyester knit fabric?
searchedAs: polyester knitted dyed fabric hs code
faqs.answer: Polyester weft-knit fabric over 30 cm wide with under 5% spandex is 6006.31 (unbleached), 6006.32 (dyed), 6006.33 (yarn-dyed) or 6006.34 (printed), all 10%; the 10-digit suffix splits nylon and polyester double knit or interlock from other constructions. Warp-knit polyester (tricot, raschel) is 6005.36–6005.39, also 10%. From China it pays 47.5% in all.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for spandex, Lycra or stretch fabric?
faqs.answer: Knit fabric over 30 cm wide with 5% or more elastomeric yarn and no rubber thread is 6004.10 (12.3%); with rubber thread it is 6004.90.20 (12.3%). Up to 30 cm wide it is 6002.40 (8% or 8.8%). Below 5% spandex the fabric is classified as an ordinary knit in 6005 or 6006, usually 10%. Woven stretch fabric is in chapters 52–55, not 60.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for jersey fabric?
searchedAs: 100 cotton single jersey fabric hs code
faqs.answer: Cotton single jersey over 30 cm wide with under 5% spandex is 6006.21–6006.24 (by finish), statistical suffix 20 "of single knit construction" — 10%. Polyester or nylon jersey is 6006.31–6006.34, suffix 80. Jersey with 5% or more spandex is 6004.10 at 12.3%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for fleece, velour, plush or faux fur fabric?
faqs.answer: Knitted pile fabric is heading 6001: long pile made by knitting in card sliver — most faux fur and sherpa — is 6001.10 (17.2% for man-made fibers); velour and plush of man-made fibers are 6001.92 (17.2%); cotton pile 6001.91 (18.5%). Brushed fleece without a true pile is classified as an ordinary knit, usually 6006 at 10%; a CBP ruling settles borderline cases.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for knit mesh or net fabric?
faqs.answer: Warp-knit mesh is reported as "open-work fabric" in 6005 (10%), or in 6004.10 (12.3%) with 5% or more spandex. Insecticide-treated mosquito-net fabric is 6005.35 (10%) and needs an EPA Notice of Arrival; finished bed nets are 6304.20. Tulle and bobbinet that are not knitted are heading 5804.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for cotton knit fabric, and what are the forced-labor rules?
faqs.answer: Cotton knit fabric over 30 cm wide is 6006.21–6006.24 (10%), or 6005.21–6005.24 if warp knit and 6001.21/6001.91 if pile. Because it is a cotton product, CBP's UFLPA guidance and the 2021 Xinjiang cotton withhold release order apply: fabric made with Xinjiang cotton is presumed barred unless the importer can trace the cotton.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on knit fabric from China?
searchedAs: tariffs on fabric from china to usa
faqs.answer: Most Chapter 60 lines from China pay 25% under Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) plus 12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31) on top of the base rate: 47.5% on 10% fabrics, up to 56% on cotton pile. Four subheadings pay only the 12.5%, 6005.35 pays 20% extra, and acrylic faux fur at ≤ $16/m² can claim an exclusion from the 25% through November 9, 2026. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Is there a U.S. tariff on imported knit fabric in 2026?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on fabric
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Chapter 60 line but one has a base rate (4%–18.5%, mostly 10%), and since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 duty applies by country: Vietnam pays 12.5% on top (22.5% on 10% fabrics); Taiwan and the EU pay 10% and Japan and Korea 12.5% in total, so their 10% knits pay little extra; China pays up to 37.5% more. USMCA and CAFTA-DR fabric that meets the yarn-forward rule is free.

faqs.question: What is the U.S. tariff on knit fabric from India?
searchedAs: tariff on textiles from india to usa
us tariff on textiles from india
textile tariffs from india to usa
faqs.answer: Indian knit fabric pays the base rate plus 10% Section 301 (9903.05.44): 20% on the 10% jersey and warp-knit lines, 22.3% on spandex fabric. India has no exception list and no Chapter 60 line offers GSP. The 2025 IEEPA duties of up to 50% ended in February 2026.

faqs.question: What is the yarn-forward rule for USMCA and CAFTA-DR knit fabric?
faqs.answer: Knit fabric is USMCA- or CAFTA-DR-originating only if it is knit in the region from regional yarn — and, for cotton and man-made fibers, regional fiber (General Notes 11 and 29). Up to 10% by weight of non-originating fiber is tolerated; spandex must be regional (USMCA allows up to 7% non-originating). Qualifying fabric enters free of the base rate and the Section 301 duty.

faqs.question: Do knit fabrics from Mexico and Canada pay tariffs?
searchedAs: tariffs on fabric from usa to canada
faqs.answer: USMCA-qualifying fabric is free: no base rate and no Section 301 duty. Non-qualifying fabric pays the base rate plus 10%. Canada's synthetic knit fabric of 6006.31–6006.33 also pays a 50% Section 338 duty, USMCA or not, since August 22, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for fabric swatches and samples?
faqs.answer: Swatches worth $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, and used only to take orders enter Free under 9811.00.60 — also outside the Section 301, China and Canada extra duties. Usable sample yardage is classified in Chapter 60 like any other fabric, and de minimis is suspended, so it pays duty.

faqs.question: How do I tell knitted fabric from woven or coated fabric for classification?
faqs.answer: Knitted fabric is made of interlocking loops (Chapter 60); woven fabric interlaces warp and weft (chapters 50–55, 58). Knit fabric that is impregnated, coated or laminated goes to chapter 59 — except pile fabric, which stays in 6001. Garments and made-up articles cut from knit fabric are chapters 61 and 63.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import knitted fabric from?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $763.3M of Chapter 60 fabric: China $158.7M, South Korea $118.3M, Israel $88.2M, India $63.5M, Mexico $60.8M. China alone supplied 21%.
